definitions.explanation: The maximum temperature recorded or forecast for a given day or period, commonly used in weather reports.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}の{最高気温|さいこうきおん}は35{度|ど}です。
{最高気温|さいこうきおん}が30{度|ど}を{超|こ}える{日|ひ}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: Days with highs exceeding 30 degrees have been continuing.

examples.japanese: {天気予報|てんきよほう}によると、{明日|あした}の{最高気温|さいこうきおん}は{今日|きょう}より5{度|ど}{低|ひく}くなるそうだ。
examples.english: According to the weather forecast, tomorrow's high will be 5 degrees lower than today's.

notes:
The standard term used in Japanese weather forecasts for the day's high temperature. Composed of {最高|さいこう} (highest) and {気温|きおん} (air temperature). Japan uses Celsius.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {最高気温|さいこうきおん}が{上|あ}がる — the high temperature rises
- {最高気温|さいこうきおん}を{記録|きろく}する — to record a maximum temperature
- {最高気温|さいこうきおん}が30{度|ど}を{超|こ}える — the high exceeds 30 degrees
- {予想|よそう}{最高気温|さいこうきおん} — forecast high temperature

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {最低気温|さいていきおん} — lowest temperature; daily low (its counterpart)
- {気温|きおん} — air temperature (general)
- {猛暑日|もうしょび} — extremely hot day (high of 35°C or above)
- {真夏日|まなつび} — midsummer day (high of 30°C or above)

USAGE:
In Japan, weather reports typically announce both {最高気温|さいこうきおん} and {最低気温|さいていきおん} for each day. Days are classified by temperature thresholds: {夏日|なつび} (25°C+), {真夏日|まなつび} (30°C+), {猛暑日|もうしょび} (35°C+).
